bugs_found: compound_interest converts principal to float, losing Decimal precision and risking float*Decimal TypeError when multiplied by Decimal expression
compound_interest mixes float principal with Decimal factor causing TypeError at runtime (float * Decimal not allowed)
loan_payment returns p/m when r==0 but p is Decimal and m is int: result type inconsistent and not rounded to currency precision
No rounding/quantization to currency minor units in compound_interest, loan_payment, apply_fee, fx_convert (financial results returned with arbitrary precision)
transfer is not atomic: if second assignment fails, source is debited without crediting destination (no rollback/transaction)
transfer compares amount (possibly float/int) with 0 and account.balance without normalizing to Decimal, risking Decimal vs float comparison errors
apply_fee computes fee = amount * pct treating pct as a raw multiplier (e.g. 0.02) but naming suggests percentage; ambiguous contract and no documentation
apply_fee can return negative net amount if fee_min > amount (min fee exceeds amount), no guard
fx_convert accepts rates dict without validating rate > 0; a zero or negative rate would silently produce wrong/zero result
fx_convert has no inverse-rate fallback nor triangulation; missing pair raises even if reverse exists
Account.balance and Receipt.amount typed as Decimal but no runtime enforcement; callers can pass float and corrupt state
Use of dataclass with mutable Decimal balance and no thread-safety/locking for transfer
compound_interest uses ** with Decimal exponent of (n*t) which is int OK, but expression order can lose precision; also no max bound on years/compounds leading to potential DoS via huge exponent
Error messages are non-localized bare strings; no custom exception hierarchy for finance domain
Docstring claims 'NO BUGS' but compound_interest has the float(principal) bug explicitly flagged in a comment
